items.headline: Google Launches AI Tool to Add Interactivity to E-books
items.excerpt: Google's Expert Intelligence lets readers query e-books bought from the Google Play store. The launch covers more than 100,000 titles, mostly trade nonfiction, from publishers including Penguin Random House and Macmillan.

items.headline: Inside the Warehouse Where Amazon Scans and Destroys Books for AI Training
items.excerpt: An interview with an employee at Amazon's AI training facility VGT3, where bought books have their spines cut off and pages scanned. Amazon declined to say whether the scans feed model training.

items.headline: AI companies are buying hardcover books and destroying them
items.excerpt: AI firms are sourcing physical books through commercial channels and pulping them after scanning. The fear for preservationists is that rare titles that can never be replaced are being destroyed for training data.

items.headline: FTC asked to investigate destruction of books
items.excerpt: More than a dozen groups have asked the Federal Trade Commission to look at the scanning and destruction of physical books for AI model training.

items.headline: Can AI Replace Your Editor? Member Q&A with Michael La Ronn and Sacha Black
items.excerpt: ALLi advisors answer indie-author questions on where AI editing actually helps and where it fails, plus IngramSpark returns and series cover consistency.

items.headline: Anthropic Adds Watermarks to Claude's AI-Generated Text
items.excerpt: Anthropic is adding watermarks to text generated by Claude, raising new questions about AI transparency, provenance and disclosure for AI-assisted books.

items.headline: How Claude watermarking works: Some accuse Anthropic of compliance theatre
items.excerpt: Commentators find it problematic that the watermark is applied when Claude is used for assistive tasks rather than purely generative ones — a distinction that matters for writers who use AI to edit.

items.headline: Amazon is buying and scanning books to train AI
items.excerpt: A sober read on the Amazon VGT3 scanning story: breathless coverage misses that many of the destroyed books may be out of date and commercially undesirable.

items.headline: Opinion: You Have More Agency Than You Think — Creative Writing and Publishing in the Age of AI
items.excerpt: Indie author Nigel George argues writers still control the craft decisions that matter in an AI-saturated market, and outlines how to build a sustainable career without chasing AI shortcuts.

items.headline: Google Play Books Book Insights has launched
items.excerpt: Google Play Books' AI-driven Book Insights has launched for thousands of select English titles. Google did not say if or when the reading tool will expand to non-English books.

items.headline: These are all of the new Spotify audiobook features
items.excerpt: A rundown of Spotify's recent audiobook push, including AI-assisted discovery such as prompt-built audiobook playlists and improved series tracking.

items.headline: Why Rights Holder Transparency Is Becoming Non-Negotiable
items.excerpt: As publishers pursue complex new licensing — including licensing works to train LLMs — opaque royalty reporting is becoming untenable. The piece argues real-time sales and payment data is now a baseline requirement.

items.headline: Around the Book World: Monday, August 24th, 2026
items.excerpt: The roundup covers Brazil's Publitik, a subscription market-intelligence platform run by AI agents, the Amazon book-scanning investigation, and German children's publisher Carlsen suing OpenAI over Das NEINhorn.

items.headline: Guest Post — Your Next Reader Is a Machine, and We Are Ready
items.excerpt: Machine readers replacing human readers can sound like a threat. The post argues publishing is already structurally prepared to make its content machine-legible — and should design for it deliberately.

items.headline: Guest Post — From Charity to Intellectual Partnership: The Global Monograph Crisis, AI, and the Future of Open Access
items.excerpt: Frances Pinter explains how Ukraine's academic publishing sector is meeting the global monograph crisis with AI-assisted production and translation, and a new open-access partnership model.

items.headline: Guest Post — AI Can Find the Article. Can It Tell Which Version It Used?
items.excerpt: In the AI era, establishing trust and validating which version of a text a model actually read depends on persistent identifiers. A practical look at provenance plumbing for publishers.
